key_insight: A fast, morphology-aware JV model can predict organic solar cell performance and stability by linking complex multi-phase morphology directly to key transport and recombination descriptors.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid screening of device architectures and degradation-sensitive morphologies, helping engineers optimize organic solar cells for both efficiency and lifetime.
method: Models up to five morphology phases: donor/acceptor, amorphous/crystalline, and mixed amorphous regions.
Uses morphology-aware inputs for light absorption, exciton dissociation, non-geminate recombination, and carrier mobilities.
Computes current-voltage curves at very low cost and compares results across materials systems.
evidence_signal: The approach was validated against Monte Carlo and 3D drift-diffusion simulations and then applied to P3HT:PCBM and PM6:Y6 to examine performance–lifetime tradeoffs.
watch_item: The morphology-performance relationship is system-dependent, so descriptors and conclusions may not transfer directly across material platforms without recalibration.
paper_title: Predicting Organic Solar Cell Performance and Stability from Fast, Morphology-aware Current-Voltage Modeling
